q-121995.name: Question 1
q-121995.worked_solution:
Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡R=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{QR}{PR}=\frac{2}{PR}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing length $PR.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}PR & =\sqrt{P{Q}^{2}+Q{R}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡R & =\frac{2}{PR}=\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122005.problem: In a right triangle $△LMN,$ $∠M$ is a right angle, $MN=\sqrt{5}$ and $LM=\sqrt{11}.$ Determine the cosine of $∠N.$
q-122005.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/df7dcd343dd2676cb38b7df3c2d8cb599fed45b9c0b25194609effe2bf27a6f7.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡N=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{MN}{LN}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{LN}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing length $LN.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}LN & =\sqrt{M{N}^{2}+L{M}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^{2}+(\sqrt{11})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5+11} \\  & =\sqrt{16} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡N & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{LN}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-122045.name: Question 3
q-122045.problem: In a right triangle $△FGH,$ $∠H$ is a right angle, $FH=2\sqrt{2}$ and $FG=6.$ Find the cosine of $∠G.$
q-122045.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14224552/assets/e585e89d11dea316c5483eeb2b2fc4750084409651ecf838e65a0d09e7bcc97f.png)

Recall the definition of cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡G=\frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}=\frac{GH}{FG}=\frac{GH}{6}
$$

Here, we need to determine the missing length $GH.$ The trick is to use the Pythagorean Theorem:

$$
\begin{aligned}GH & =\sqrt{F{G}^{2}-F{H}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}-(2\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36-8} \\  & =\sqrt{28} \\  & =2\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡G & =\frac{GH}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{7}}{6} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡N=\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}=\frac{OM}{MN}=\frac{OM}{2.5}

$$
\begin{aligned}OM & =\sqrt{O{N}^{2}-M{N}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{6.5}^{2}-{2.5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{42.25-6.25} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6\end{aligned}

\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡N & =\frac{OM}{2.5} \\  & =\frac{6}{2.5} \\  & =\frac{60}{25} \\  & =\frac{12}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
